Home.heading: Claude Code themes, with previews and one-command install
Home.lead: A collection of desktop animated themes and CLI color themes. Every entry shows its version requirement and, for desktop mods, the permissions it uses.
Home.addMarketplaceHelp: Run this in a Claude Code session. After that, any theme here installs with a single command.
Home.desktopCardBody: Colors and an animated backdrop behind the conversation in the Claude desktop app. {count} themes.
Home.cliCardBody: Color schemes for the Claude Code terminal, applied with /theme. {count} themes.
Home.step1Body: Check the preview, the required Claude Code version, and the permissions.
Home.step2Body: Run the marketplace command once. It registers ThemeCC as a plugin source.
Home.step3Body: Run the install command. For a CLI theme, pick it with /theme. For a desktop theme, start a new local session in the Code tab.
Home.safetyBody: Mods run on your machine with the same access as Claude Code. They are not sandboxed. Every desktop theme here is pinned to one commit and reviewed before it is listed. Read the review notes on each page.
Home.submitBody: Open a pull request on GitHub. CLI themes are merged once checks pass. Desktop mods are reviewed by hand.

List.desktopLead: Desktop themes are mods. They color the Code tab of the Claude desktop app and can draw an animated backdrop behind the conversation. They work in local desktop sessions only. The terminal does not draw backdrops.
List.cliLead: CLI themes recolor the Claude Code terminal interface: accent, status colors, diffs, and borders. They do not change your terminal background or the main text color. Pick one with /theme.
List.desktopReq: Backdrops need Claude Code {backdrop} or later. Colors in the Code tab need {colors} or later.
List.cliReq: Custom themes need Claude Code {version} or later.
List.emptyRegistry: No themes have been listed in this category yet.

Theme.activateDesktop: Start a new local session in the Code tab. The mod applies its theme when the session starts. Use one theme mod at a time: each one replaces the previous theme.
Theme.activateCli: Run /theme and pick {name}. If it is your first custom theme, restart Claude Code once.
Theme.singleFileBody: This puts the JSON file into ~/.claude/themes without the plugin system.
Theme.author: Author
Theme.permissionsLead: Declared by the maintainers after reading the source at the pinned commit.
Theme.modWarning: This is a mod. It runs with the same access as Claude Code and is not sandboxed. To see what it does before you install it, clone its repository and run claude plugin validate on the directory. The hooks and calls lines list its events and requests.
Theme.previewHint: Preview images and videos belong to the theme's author.
Theme.terminalNote: Approximate rendering from the theme's color values. Final colors depend on your terminal and the {base} base theme.
Theme.contrastNote: Contrast is estimated against an assumed {background} terminal background. Values that depend on your terminal palette (ansi) are not scored.

Theme.unofficialPort: Community port. Not made or endorsed by the original project.

Submit.heading: Submit a theme
Submit.lead: Themes are added through a pull request to the ThemeCC repository. There is no account and no form.
Submit.step1: Fork the repository and create a folder under registry/desktop or registry/cli, named with your theme's slug.
Submit.step3: Run pnpm registry:check locally. It runs the same checks as the pull request.
Submit.step4: Open a pull request. CI validates the entry. A maintainer merges CLI themes after checks pass and reviews desktop mods by hand.
Submit.desktopBody: Your theme stays in your own repository. The entry points to it with a full commit hash. To update it, open a new pull request with the new hash.
Submit.desktopFiles: registry/desktop/<slug>/theme.json, poster.webp (up to 300 KB), preview.mp4 (optional, up to 8 MB and 15 seconds)
Submit.desktopRule1: The repository must be public and have an accepted license.
Submit.desktopRule2: The plugin name must equal the slug.
Submit.desktopRule3: The plugin must pass claude plugin validate.
Submit.desktopRule4: No obfuscated or minified code. Declare network, file, and command use honestly.
Submit.desktopRule5: You must own the preview artwork or have permission to use it.
Submit.desktopRule6: Keep the reviewed field as in the example. The maintainer who reviews your pull request replaces it.
Submit.cliBody: The theme file uses the official Claude Code format, so it works if you copy it to ~/.claude/themes.
Submit.cliRule1: theme.json has name, base, and overrides. Colors use #rrggbb, #rgb, rgb(), ansi256(), or ansi:name.
Submit.cliRule2: meta.json states the author and an accepted license. Ports of existing palettes must name the upstream project and keep its copyright notice.
Submit.cliRule3: A description written in your own words.
Submit.licensesBody: {licenses}. Entries without a clear license are not listed.
Submit.reviewBody: CLI themes only contain color values, so they are merged after the automated checks pass. Desktop mods can read files, make requests, and run commands, so a maintainer reads the source at the pinned commit before merging and records the result in the entry.
Submit.removalBody: Authors can ask for an entry to be removed at any time by opening an issue or a pull request.
